articles.title: Lebanon: Fragments: Explosive Weapons Monitor Quarterly (Vol. 4, Issue 1, October 2026)
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. Fragments is a series of short articles from the Explosive Weapons Monitor, a research initiative of the International Network on Explosive Weapons (INEW), on the use and impact of explosive weapons in populated areas. This issue looks at how evidence of civilian harm from explosive weapons in populated areas can be put to use. In the first article, Article 36 and the Explosive Weapons Monitor analyse that 81 States are both Parties or Signatories to the Arms Trade Treaty and endorsers of the Political Declaration on explosive weapons in populated areas. Citing patterns of harm in Gaza, Lebanon and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, they argue that this evidence should inform the risk assessments States must carry out under Article 7 of the Treaty before authorising arms exports, and set out practical steps to bring implementation of the two instruments closer together. The article was first published as Chapter 1 of the ATT Monitor 2026. The second piece is a methodological guide developed by the Explosive Weapons Monitor, Kobo and Physicians for Human Rights. Drawing mainly on examples from Ukraine, it sets out indicators for documenting the effects of attacks on energy infrastructure on physical and mental health, education, livelihoods and other areas of civilian life, linked to available sources of data. It is intended for researchers and analysts working in humanitarian, human rights and civilian protection, and may also assist justice and accountability bodies.

articles.title: Runner, 24, Dies 2 Miles From NYC Marathon Finish Line
articles.description: A 24-year-old New York City Marathon runner died after collapsing two miles from the finish line. Rachel Apa was running her first marathon on Sunday to raise money for Parkinson’s disease research, in honor of her late grandfather. “My grandfather was one of my role models growing up,” she wrote on LinkedIn. “He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges.” The former Bucknell University field hockey player had been training for months. Her father told The New York Times that she was in “perfect health, perfect shape.” Apa collapsed near Mile 24, in Central Park, and was rushed to the hospital, where she died from rhabdomyolysis, a rare injury where muscles break down rapidly and leak a toxic protein into the bloodstream. The New York Road Runners told The Times that the last time a runner at the marathon died after a medical incident was in 2024. Read it at The New York Times Read more at The Daily Beast.
